definitions.explanation: Describes a cliff, rock face, or slope that rises or drops almost vertically, as if cut with a blade. Used as an attributive modifier before nouns.

examples.japanese: {道|みち}の{両側|りょうがわ}に{切|き}り{立|た}った{岩壁|がんぺき}がそびえていた。
examples.english: Sheer rock walls towered on both sides of the road.

examples.japanese: {切|き}り{立|た}った{断崖|だんがい}の{上|うえ}から{海|うみ}を{見下|みお}ろした。
examples.english: I looked down at the sea from atop a precipitous cliff.

notes:
The past-tense form of the compound verb {切|き}り{立|た}つ (to rise steeply), used almost exclusively as an attributive adjective modifying nouns. The image is of rock that looks as though it has been cleanly cut ({切|き}る) and stands upright ({立|た}つ).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {切|き}り{立|た}った{崖|がけ}: a sheer cliff
- {切|き}り{立|た}った{岩|いわ}: a steep rock face
- {切|き}り{立|た}った{断崖|だんがい}: a precipitous cliff
- {切|き}り{立|た}った{山肌|やまはだ}: a steep mountainside

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {険|けわ}しい: steep, rugged — more general; can also mean severe or stern
- {急峻|きゅうしゅん}な: precipitous, very steep — formal, literary
- {断崖絶壁|だんがいぜっぺき}: sheer precipice — a set noun phrase for a cliff with no footholds
